hints: Calculate the maximum cruising speed: $v = at = 2.1 \times 5 = 10.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Identify the time milestones: $t = 0\text{ s}$, $t = 5\text{ s}$, $t = 5 + 24 = 29\text{ s}$, and $t = 29 + 6 = 35\text{ s}$.
The velocity-time graph is a trapezium with parallel sides of length $24\text{ s}$ and $35\text{ s}$, and height $10.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Calculate the total distance as the area of the trapezium: $\text{Distance} = \frac{1}{2}(24 + 35) \times 10.5$.
walkthrough:
Find the maximum speed reached by the bus after accelerating from rest for $5\text{ s}$:
$$v_{\text{max}} = u + at = 0 + 2.1(5) = 10.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Identify the key coordinates for the velocity-time graph:
- Acceleration phase from $(0, 0)$ to $(5, 10.5)$.
- Constant speed cruising phase from $(5, 10.5)$ to $(29, 10.5)$, since $t = 5 + 24 = 29\text{ s}$.
- Deceleration phase from $(29, 10.5)$ down to rest at $(35, 0)$, since $t = 29 + 6 = 35\text{ s}$.

Evaluate the total distance between the bus stops from the area of the trapezium:
$$\text{Distance} = \frac{1}{2}(b_1 + b_2)h = \frac{1}{2}(24 + 35) \times 10.5$$
$$\text{Distance} = \frac{1}{2}(59) \times 10.5 = 29.5 \times 10.5 = 309.75\text{ m} \approx 310\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Calculate the maximum speed attained by the bus at the end of the acceleration phase:
$$v = u + at$$
Substitute $u = 0$, $a = 2.1\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $t = 5\text{ s}$:
$$v = 0 + 2.1 \times 5 = 10.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Determine the key time intervals:
- Stage 1 (Acceleration): from $t = 0$ to $t = 5\text{ s}$, rising linearly from $v = 0$ to $v = 10.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
- Stage 2 (Cruising): from $t = 5$ to $t = 5 + 24 = 29\text{ s}$, remaining horizontal at $v = 10.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
- Stage 3 (Deceleration): from $t = 29$ to $t = 29 + 6 = 35\text{ s}$, falling linearly from $v = 10.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $0\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Sketch the graph: plot the vertices $(0, 0)$, $(5, 10.5)$, $(29, 10.5)$, and $(35, 0)$ connected by straight lines on axes of velocity ($v$) against time ($t$).

Calculate the total distance travelled as the area of the trapezium:
$$\text{Area} = \frac{a + b}{2} \times h$$
where $a = 24\text{ s}$ (top parallel edge), $b = 35\text{ s}$ (bottom parallel edge), and $h = 10.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ (height):
$$\text{Distance} = \frac{24 + 35}{2} \times 10.5 = \frac{59}{2} \times 10.5 = 29.5 \times 10.5$$
Calculate intermediate multiplication:
$$29.5 \times 10.5 = 29.5 \times 10 + 29.5 \times 0.5 = 295 + 14.75 = 309.75\text{ m}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $310\text{ m}$.
